{'index': 0, 'translation': 'In response to climate change and rising disaster risks, the Hong Kong Red Cross today (30th) released the "Hong Kong Disaster Risk and Response Capacity Map 2026" study, assessing the risks faced by various districts in Hong Kong against typhoons, extreme heat, and fires. The report shows that over half of all districts in Hong Kong face high risk from two to three types of disasters simultaneously, while 14.7% of districts are at extreme disaster risk, mainly concentrated in Yuen Long and North District. In addition, parts of the New Territories are notably affected by "hot days," with 76% of districts across Hong Kong facing extreme heat risks; fire risk is also highly concentrated in Yau Tsim Mong, a densely populated area with a high proportion of low-income families. The Red Cross recommends that various sectors refer to the risk map for future planning, grasp the disaster risks of each district earlier, and incorporate disaster preparedness projects into the development blueprint.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': '14.7% of districts are at extreme disaster risk, concentrated in Yuen Long and North District'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': "The Hong Kong Red Cross commissioned a third-party organisation to conduct a questionnaire survey to understand the public's disaster response capabilities; integrating data on population, public facilities, meteorological conditions, and socio-economic factors from Small Planning Statistics Areas, the research was conducted from four aspects, including: the community distribution affected by climate and disasters; the disaster preparedness and resilience of each district; the trends of threats from extreme heat, fires, and typhoons; and the gap between community needs and current support."}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'The survey found that over half (52.6%) of all districts in Hong Kong face high-risk threats from two to three types of disasters simultaneously. Some 14.7% of districts are at extreme disaster risk, mainly located in parts of Yuen Long and North District. Among them, Lau Fau Shan, San Tin, and Shap Pat Heung in Yuen Long District occupy the top five positions in the "highest overall risk areas"; in terms of typhoon disasters, Lam Tsuen in Tai Po carries the highest risk, followed by Tai O, with other high-risk areas also including Lau Fau Shan, San Tin, and Shap Pat Heung; San Tin in Yuen Long also ranks second in extreme heat risk.'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'Yau Tsim Mong has the highest fire risk, with only 30% of residents having participated in fire drills'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'After the Wang Fuk Court fire, fire risk in Hong Kong has drawn much attention. The report points out that fire risk is highly concentrated, with the top five highest-risk areas all located in Yau Tsim Mong, involving factors such as dense population, high proportion of low-income families, and a low number of first-aid facilities. However, the survey shows that over 70% of citizens have not participated in any fire drill in the past year, with participation rates particularly low in some extreme fire-risk areas such as Kowloon City and Sham Shui Po, at only 23.2% and 29.6% respectively, while Yau Tsim Mong stands at just 33.3%.'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'Yu Hoi-si, Head of Institutional Planning and Humanitarian Diplomacy at the Red Cross, stated that the low drill participation rate is a potential risk factor that may increase the likelihood of fires in a district, and recommended that the drill participation rate of residents in individual districts be improved first. The organisation will provide home improvement works and organise disaster prevention training workshops, helping residents establish mutual aid groups to foster connection and support, in order to address the fire risks faced by districts.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'The report points out that fire risk is highly concentrated, with the top five highest-risk areas all located in Yau Tsim Mong, involving factors such as dense population and a high proportion of low-income families.'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'Typhoons frequently hit Hong Kong; shelters far from North District and Yuen Long'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': 'In recent years, typhoons have struck Hong Kong frequently, and the survey also found that parts of North District and Yuen Long are located far from temporary typhoon shelters. Among them, Pat Heung in Yuen Long, Sha Tau Kok and Shuen Wan in North District are over 3,000 metres from typhoon shelters, which is 3.5 times and 4.2 times the citywide average distance respectively. The Red Cross recommends reviewing the coverage, location, and facilities of typhoon shelters to enable citizens to evacuate in a timely manner before typhoons arrive, ensuring safety of life; and pre-positioning supplies in high-risk communities or temporary shelters before severe weather, providing emergency support and first-aid services to high-risk communities during severe weather.'}

{'index': 10, 'translation': 'Under extreme weather, citizens are also affected by extreme heat. Some 42% of districts in Hong Kong face high extreme heat risk, while 34% face extreme extreme heat risk. In 2025, the annual number of very hot days in Hong Kong was 53, and hot nights numbered 54; however, the survey shows that parts of the New Territories have notably higher "hot day" figures, with San Tin and Kwu Tung recording a combined 103 "hot days," nearly double the citywide figure; other severely affected areas include Lai Tak Tsuen, Choi Hung, and Hung Hom, which recorded 73, 66, and 53 "hot days" respectively. Kowloon continues to be affected by "hot nights," with Hung Hom recording 54 "hot nights" last year.'}

{'index': 11, 'translation': 'Yu Hoi-si pointed out that severe extreme heat is mainly concentrated in the northern New Territories, while some densely populated areas in Kowloon and Hong Kong Island are also at extreme risk. The organisation will provide cooling supplies, promote heat prevention information, and make good use of community spaces in high-risk areas to set up temporary rest stations for citizens to "cool off from the heat."'}

{'index': 12, 'translation': 'Red Cross recommends strengthening risk management in the northern New Territories'}

{'index': 13, 'translation': 'Yu Hoi-si pointed out that there are "natural factors" behind some districts becoming high-risk areas, but at the same time there are also hardware and software reasons. She hopes the government can make good use of data and information to "prescribe the right remedy" and meet the real needs of citizens. Red Cross Secretary General Lin Chuan-peng said that understanding disasters is "only the first step"; responses must be tailored to the different problems of different districts. She expects the risk map will help various sectors grasp the disaster risks of districts earlier in the initial planning of new communities, and incorporate disaster prevention and preparedness projects into the development blueprint.'}

{'index': 14, 'translation': 'The Red Cross has put forward four major recommendations, including: strengthening risk management awareness and disaster prevention planning in the northern New Territories; enhancing district-based heat prevention strategies in response to the distribution of hot days and hot nights; increasing fire drills in high fire-risk areas and improving citizen participation; and improving the coverage, facilities, and equipment of temporary typhoon shelters.'}
